chapter: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
title: Lang and Venuti on the records and why they failed commercially
summary: Eddie Lang and Joe Venuti were brought in for recordings, and Challis explains how the band's records made no hits.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So only with musicians did we cut any ice and they used to come up there quite a bit. But, of course, they came

up to listen to Bix and Trumbauer and Don Murray and Spiegel was in the band then. Spiegel used to have some kind of jug tone, and he played a megaphone and he'd play these melodic tunes and waltzes and he used to eat those things up. They liked that. He was the commercial part of our band.
You said they brought in Lang and Venuti.

Right, and then I would just leave out a part. They would bring in the singers and they would never call up and say, 'Look, they're going to sing this in such and such a key.' But they would just bring in the singer and I would have the arrangement made and they would say, 'We will cut here, play the verse and before you go into the chorus, Eddie, get us into the key you want and Joe, you and Eddie play the backup, in back of the voices.' You never could tell. We couldn't --unless I could get the part, the rhythm parts written out in harmony, you only heard it from Eddie. He was very predominate on the things, but they were a big help, these two guys, and so we didn't have too much trouble recording. We didn't have any rejected, or come back and make it again.
So as far as the recording was concerned, I would say that they didn't accomplish what they set out to accomplish.
They didn't have any hit tunes there. At least they didn't turn out to be hits.
